title: Small's Paradise and Charlie Johnson's band
summary: Ed Small's club, a run-in with a gangster over a showgirl, and Charlie Johnson.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: And I associated and I met plenty of people, and there was Ed Small. He was boss of -- he owned Small's Paradise. Charlie Johnson was in there, had the band for years. Charlie and I became very good friends. I used to go in there, and one time there was a showgirl that I took up there once, and some gangster up there, Jerry Preston, he was after her or something like that. And somebody said that she was in there, going to Small's Paradise with Scottie, the trumpet player. We just went in there one night, there was a bunch of us together, from the show.

And Jerry made a remark that I'm coming after him. And it came to me. And Ed Small heard about it. He's the boss. Well, he sent word to me that -- come on in there whenever you want, Scottie, Jerry ain't coming after anybody. And I knew all the fellows in the band, in Charlie Johnson's band. And I could have played in his band, but I was working.
And we became very good friends.
Oh, he had a good band. Yeah, he had a good band. Most of those guys are gone, too. I went to their funerals. Lord, I've been to more funerals of musicians. So many, so many.
